extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry and readers of IUT (inter-universal Teichmüller) theory
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions and reconstruction/rigidity criteria in Inter-Universal Teichmüller theory: pseudo-monoids, (Kummer)-coric rational functions, coric structures, Kummer isomorphisms, and three kinds of cyclotomic rigidity, together with algorithmic/group-theoretic reconstruction procedures and the mono-anabelian transport technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topological pseudo-monoid (Definition 9.1(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A topological space P with a continuous map S :PP SP is a topological pseudo-monoid if there exists a topological abelian group M and an embedding : P  M such that S = { (a,b)PP | (a)_(b) ( P )  M } and the restriction of M's group operation to S gives the map S P.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the base structural requirement: P must embed into a multiplicative topological abelian group M so that the given binary map on P is the restriction of M's multiplication to the image of P. The definition is explicit about topology and embedding; this is the object one calls simply a 'pseudo-monoid' if M is discrete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discrete pseudo-monoid (Definition 9.1(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: If M in the above is equipped with the discrete topology, then P is referred to simply as a pseudo-monoid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This single-sentence variant marks the discrete/topological distinction and is used when no topology beyond discrete is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisible pseudo-monoid (Definition 9.1(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A pseudo-monoid P is divisible if there exist M and embedding as above such that for any n 1 and a in M there exists b in M with b^n = a, and for any n 1 and a in M, a in image(P) iff a^n in image(P).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisibility requires both that M be divisible (every element has n-th roots) and that membership of image(P) is preserved under taking powers, ensuring the pseudo-monoid behaves like a divisible subgroup in M.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclotomic pseudo-monoid (Definition 9.1(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A pseudo-monoid P is cyclotomic if there exist M and embedding as above such that the torsion subgroup M_tors of M is isomorphic to Q/Z, and M_tors  image(P) and M_tors  image(P)^{(1)}  image(P) hold (i.e., torsion sits inside the image and certain torsion-compatibility conditions hold).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This isolates the cyclotomic flavour: the ambient group M must have torsion equal to Q/Z and that torsion is captured inside P's image. This condition is used repeatedly to set up cyclotomes and Kummer-theoretic identifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclotome bZ(P) (Definition 9.1(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: For a cyclotomic pseudo-monoid P, define bZ(P) := Hom(Q/Z, P) and call it the cyclotome of P.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cyclotome is the Hom-group from Q/Z into P and is the key object for comparing cyclotomic structures and for formulating cyclotomic-rigidity isomorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical and strictly critical points (Definition 9.2(1,2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A closed point of the proper smooth curve determined by a finite subextension of LC is a critical point if it maps to a closed point of the coarse scheme jCLj arising from one of the 2-torsion points of EF_mod. A critical point is strictly critical if it does not map to the closed point arising from the unique cusp of CL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These geometric notions identify the finite set of points where coricity conditions impose value constraints; strictly critical points are those relevant for the root-of-unity condition in coric functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: (Kummer)-coric rational function (Definition 9.2(3) with (a)-(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A rational function f in LC is (Kummer)-coric if (a) if f /\ L then f has precisely one pole (any order) and at least two distinct zeroes over L; (b) the divisor of zeroes and divisor of poles are defined over a finite extension of L(15) and avoid the critical points; (c) the values of f at any strictly critical point of jCLj are roots of unity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coric functions are singled out by precise divisor and value conditions. These properties make such functions distinguish zeros and poles (useful for Kummer-theoretic reconstructions) and are central to building the cyclotomic pseudo-monoids used later.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1(Kummer)-coric and 1(Kummer)(2)-coric functions (Definition 9.2(4,5))
rubrics_metrics.description: f is 1(Kummer)-coric if some positive integer n 1 has f^n (Kummer)-coric. f is 1(Kummer)(2)-coric if there is c  U such that c^{-1} f is 1(Kummer)-coric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These weakenings allow passing to powers or scalar multiples (by units) to realize coricity; the distinctions are important when forming divisible or cyclotomic pseudo-monoids of such functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coric function sets form (divisible cyclotomic) pseudo-monoids (Remark 9.2.1(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of (Kummer)-coric functions (LC) forms a pseudo-monoid; the sets of 1(Kummer)-coric and 1(Kummer)(2)-coric functions form divisible cyclotomic pseudo-monoids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies the algebraic structure of each class of coric functions and motivates treating them as Frobenius-like or etale-like objects in reconstruction arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1(Kummer)-coric and 1(Kummer)(2)-coric structures on Frobenioids (Definition 9.6(1),(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: An 1(Kummer)-coric (resp. 1(Kummer)(2)-coric) structure on a pre-Frobenioid yF~ is the data of isomorphs of the corresponding (Frobenius-like) pseudo-monoids M~_{1(Kummer)}(yD) (resp. M~_{1(Kummer)(2)}) and of the (etale-like) pseudo-monoids with continuous (y~)rat-action; the pair is considered as cyclotomic pseudo-monoids with (y~)rat-action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such structures package the Frobenius-like and etale-like realizations of the (Kummer)-coric pseudo-monoids together with group actions; their existence and uniqueness up to canonical isomorphism are used to regard yF~ as being equipped with these structures tacitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence and uniqueness of cyclotome isomorphisms characterized by Kummer isomorphisms (Cyc. Rig. NF1 & NF2)
rubrics_metrics.description: There exist unique isomorphisms bZ(y(5))  (22)(2)  (24)! (22)bZ(yM~_{1(Kummer)}) (and variants) characterised as those that induce the corresponding Kummer isomorphisms yM~_{1(Kummer)} Kum (24)(0)! M~_{1(Kummer)}(yD).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These 'cyclotomic rigidity' statements assert canonical identifications between cyclotomes arising from etale-like and Frobenius-like objects, determined uniquely by requiring compatibility with Kummer classes. They are used to canonically relate otherwise a priori unrelated multiplicative structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local/global analogues of cyclotomic rigidity (Cyc. Rig. NF3 & NF4)
rubrics_metrics.description: For local (non-Archimedean and Archimedean) contexts, analogous unique isomorphisms between cyclotomes exist and are characterised by inducing local Kummer isomorphisms (e.g., yM_{1(Kummer),v} Kum (24)(0)! M_{1(Kummer),v}(yDv), etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The same uniqueness/characterization principle applies locally; the paper emphasizes constructing these isomorphisms for v-adic and Archimedean Frobenioids and for corresponding etale-like objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kummer isomorphism / Kummer-theoretic injections
rubrics_metrics.description: There are natural injections from Frobenius-like pseudo-monoids into H^1-limits (Kummer classes) and Kummer isomorphisms between yM-objects and M(yD)-objects; Kummer isomorphisms identify multiplicative monoids via induced maps on Kummer classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Kummer maps/injections are the concrete mechanism by which cyclotome isomorphisms are required to act: the cyclotome isomorphism is chosen so that it induces the Kummer isomorphism on the appropriate direct limits of cohomology modules. This requirement determines uniqueness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group-theoretic reconstructability of function fields, pseudo-monoids, and evaluations (Lemma 9.3, Def 9.4, Example 9.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: From the profinite group y(5) (or categories yD}), one can group-theoretically reconstruct isomorphs of pro-finite groups corresponding to X_K, the function field of X_K, pseudo-monoids of (Kummer)-coric functions, evaluations at strictly critical points, valuation sets V(yD~), and monoids of stack-theoretic arithmetic divisors; these reconstructions extend to produce global non-realized Frobenioids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes the algorithmic/group-theoretic reconstruction program: given the abstract (profinite) group or category, one recovers multiplicative and geometric objects (fields, monoids, valuations) necessary to define cyclotomes and Kummer maps. It is presented as a stepwise procedure and is central to the IUT-style reconstruction arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mono-anabelian transport (Remark 9.6.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given pro-finite groups y(5), z(5) isomorphic to (5)X and isomorphs of the associated etale-like and Frobenius-like multiplicative objects, one can canonically relate the multiplicative structures (yO(3), zO(3) or yM~, zM~) by using Kummer theory made available via cyclotomic rigidity; this canonical relation is called mono-anabelian transport.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mono-anabelian transport is the technique to 'transport' multiplicative/algebraic structures between two isomorphic underlying topological groups by passing through cyclotomes and Kummer isomorphisms. The method requires cyclotomic rigidity to make the Kummer-theoretic identifications canonical (up to specified torsors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on selecting among three cyclotomic rigidities (Remark 9.6.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three cyclotomic rigidities are used in IUT: (LCFT) cyclotomic rigidity via local class field theory for constant monoids at local places in V_good \ V_non (unit portion); (Mono-th.) cyclotomic rigidity of mono-theta environment for theta functions and their evaluations at local places in V_bad (value-group portion); (NF2) cyclotomic rigidity via Q_{>0}\bZ(2)= {1} for non-realized global Frobenioids (global realized portion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is prescriptive guidance: use LCFT-rigidity at V_good \ V_non where unit-portions are shared under (2)-links; avoid LCFT at V_bad because value-group portions are deformed there; use mono-theta rigidity at V_bad because it only uses the N-portion and is compatible across Hodge theatres; use NF2 for global non-realized portions. The explanation clarifies which part of (2)-links each rigidity controls and why particular rigidities are chosen for multiradial algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness up to bZ(2)-torsor indeterminacy and acceptance of bZ(2)-indeterminacy for multiradial algorithms
rubrics_metrics.description: Isomorphisms between cyclotomes form a bZ(2)-torsor; in situations where the value-group portion is not shared under (2)-links, one admits bZ(2)-indeterminacy to make algorithms multiradial (e.g., in use of LCFT-rigidity in V_good \ V_non).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a procedural/acceptance criterion: the presence of bZ(2)-indeterminacy is acknowledged and exploited to achieve multi-radiality in algorithms; where this indeterminacy would break cross-Hodge-theatre compatibility, alternative rigidities (mono-theta) are used.
